subject: Scaling window offsets & sprint credits for Dedicated migration
messages:
From: Eva Morales <eva.morales@fluxdata.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@fluxdata.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Migrating API traffic to Dedicated — timing & credits?

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — FluxData is excited about the latency improvements we saw. We are lining up a migration window that matches our engineering sprints (two-week cadence) and I wanted to clarify a few commercial details before we lock dates with procurement.

Quick list:
- Conversion credits: do you offer an upfront credit that offsets hosted spend during the first 8 weeks after cutover? If so, how is it sized and applied (monthly amortization vs. one-off)?
- Bridge months: we have a hard launch in early July; would Redwood consider a 4–6 week bridge where we get reserved throughput guarantees but can still scale down if we miss adoption targets?
- Commit sizing & SLA: our traffic is spiky — we need to understand how GPU pool sizing maps to throughput guarantees (tokens/sec or concurrent requests) and any shortfall true-up mechanics.

Procurement asked for a simple example (numbers) so they can compare against other offers. I've attached our migration requirements doc. Can you put together a one-pager or a short schedule we can share internally?

Best,
Eva
Director of Core Platform
FluxData
(Attachment: FluxData_migration_requirements.pdf (PDF, 92KB))
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Eva Morales <eva.morales@fluxdata.com>, Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@fluxdata.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migrating API traffic to Dedicated — timing & credits?

Eva / Alejandro —

Great questions. Below is a practical, runnable approach we use for customers on a sprint-driven cutover. I attached a short conversion_timetable.xlsx with an example amortization schedule and a sample credit calculation.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Phased handoff: 6-week phased onramp (we call it a "scaling window"). Weeks 1–2: shadow traffic + KV prefix caching. Weeks 3–6: progressive routing (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with guaranteed reserved throughput turned on at Week 3.
- Sprint credits: conversion credit equal to 50% of your average hosted spend in the prior 3 months, paid as a monthly offset across the 6-week window (applied as invoice credits). We can do either a 6-week straight amortization or front-load 60% to the first invoice and 40% to the second — happy to align to FluxData's accounting preference.
- Bridge months & soft-commit: we recommend a 2-month soft-commit after cutover where you have access to burst pool capacity and a defined shortfall true-up. During the soft commit we cap true-ups at 30% of committed throughput to avoid surprise bills.
- Throughput guarantees: we guarantee median P95 token latency for the committed throughput band. Practically, we size GPU pools using target concurrent sessions and per-request expected token lengths — see the attached workbook for worked examples. Shortfalls above the cap translate to either credits (if we miss SLA) or a true-up charge (if you exceed committed footprint); exact thresholds are in the workbook.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share the XLS with a worked example keyed to the numbers you send.
2) Marissa and Karthik will confirm commercial guardrails and any partner marketplace constraints.
3) If that looks good, we put a 2-page term sheet in front of procurement and a one-page migration playbook for engineering.

If you want, we can lock a tentative cutover week now and make the credits conditional on signing a soft-commit by the pre-cutover review (reduces administrative churn).

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: conversion_timetable.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 24KB))
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Migrating API traffic to Dedicated — timing & credits?

Looping Karthik for commercial approval. A few internal notes:
- The 50%-of-hosted baseline is reasonable for enterprise deals but we should confirm FluxData's hosted spend window (90-day avg) and whether they have any prior overage credits.
- I support the 2-month soft-commit with a 30% cap on true-ups — it protects both sides while giving FluxData breathing room.
- We should propose two payment/credit options in the term sheet: straight amortization across the 6-week scaling window, or 60/40 front-load. Ops prefers front-load for Q2 recognition but finance may push back.

Action items for Karthik: can you sign off on the cap and the two amortization options? Also confirm any legal constraints on conditional credits in marketplace deals.

—Marissa
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: Eva Morales <eva.morales@fluxdata.com>, Alejandro Ruiz <alejandro@fluxdata.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Migrating API traffic to Dedicated — timing & credits?

Eva / Alejandro —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per internal alignment here is a tidy summary you can put in front of procurement and engineering:

1) Scaling window (6 weeks):
   - Weeks 1–2: shadow mode + KV prefix caching. No billing impact beyond hosted baseline.
   - Week 3: enable reserved throughput at 25% routing (committed capacity live).
   - Weeks 4–6: ramp to 100% routing by Week 6.

2) Conversion credit (example):
   - Size: 50% of your 90-day hosted average (example numbers in attached XLS).
   - Application: applied as invoice credit across the 6-week window; default amortization is equal installments, optional 60/40 front-load on request.

3) Soft-commit & bridge months:
   - 2-month soft-commit post-cutover with access to burst pool.
   - True-up cap: 30% of committed throughput during soft-commit window.

4) SLA mechanics:
   - Throughput guarantees mapped to committed concurrent sessions + P95 token latency. Missed SLA => credit to customer; sustained overage => true-up invoiced or move to higher commit tier after review.

Attachments: migration_playbook_v1.pdf (one-page runbook) and conversion_timetable.xlsx (worked example with numbers).

If this looks good I can convert it into a 2-page term summary for procurement and drop a migration playbook into your team's Drive folder. Would you like us to target the week of July 5 for cutover (that gives both teams four sprint cycles to prep)?

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(Attachments: migration_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 78KB); conversion_timetable.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 24KB))
